rows.citation: Appukuttan S, Davison AP (2022). Reproducing and quantitatively validating a biologically-constrained point-neuron model of CA1 pyramidal cells. Frontiers in Integrative Neuroscience, 16:1041423.
rows.model_type: Izhikevich-type point-neuron CA1 pyramidal models (original Brian; reimplemented in Brian2 and NEURON); not NeuroML
rows.controlled_mutations: no; compares independent reimplementations, not deliberately seeded single faults; initial-voltage changes explored only as side checks.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; ranges of depolarizing current steps for f-I profiles, hyperpolarizing steps, and an I-V curve test.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes; features extracted with eFEL through the eFELunit SciUnit test suite, compared by RMSE.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; tests reproduce original-study figures plus added characterisation tests; no protocol selection or minimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; single model family, no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; manual reimplementation from the published article.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Documents cross-simulator discrepancies with eFEL-based SciUnit tests. NeuroSem would add seeded single-fault mutants, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy battery selection, and held-out model and mutation-family evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fnint.2022.1041423; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 36424953); PMC9679150 full-text XML via Europe PMC; PyPI JSON for efelunit; GitHub REST API for Ferguson2014_Repro.

rows.citation: Gutzen R, von Papen M, Trensch G, et al. (2018). Reproducible Neural Network Simulations: Statistical Methods for Model Validation on the Level of Network Activity Data. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12:90.
rows.model_type: spiking neural network (Izhikevich polychronization model) in C versus SpiNNaker neuromorphic implementation
rows.controlled_mutations: partial; tracks real implementation iterations (step size, fixed-point arithmetic, threshold-detection fix), not deliberately seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; a single recorded random external input drives the network; no stimulation-protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; network spike statistics (firing rates, variability, correlations) with effect sizes and hypothesis tests; not single-cell eFEL features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; validation measures are chosen by hand.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; one model and its reproduction, no held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted or automated model transformations are studied.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Model-to-model equivalence testing at network-activity level. NeuroSem targets single-cell current-clamp behaviour, seeded mutants, numerically calibrated tolerances, and optimised protocol batteries with held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2018.00090; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 30618696); PMC6305903 full-text XML via Europe PMC; GitHub REST API for INM-6/NetworkUnit.

rows.citation: Dictus H, Subert E, Romani A, et al. (2026). pyRMV: Reusable, Cross-model Validation for Computational Science. arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.09956.
rows.model_type: general computational models; validation suite applied to a mouse primary visual cortex circuit model
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no fault seeding or mutation analysis described.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; validations mainly cover spontaneous activity; stimulus passed as data arguments rather than as a protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; population-level properties such as firing rates and connectivity statistics, not single-cell eFEL features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; no protocol selection or test minimisation described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; no discovery/held-out model split described.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted or automated model transformations are studied.
rows.software: pyRMV https://github.com/HDictus/pyRMV (code link from arXiv HTML; no licence detected by GitHub API; README titled Analysis-neuro)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Model-agnostic validation against experimental data. NeuroSem instead does model-to-mutant regression under current-clamp protocols, with mutant-calibrated battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page and HTML full text (v1 submitted 2026-07-21); DataCite API for DOI 10.48550/arxiv.2608.09956; GitHub REST API (repo, contents, README).

rows.citation: Cooper J, Mirams GR, Niederer SA (2011). High-throughput functional curation of cellular electrophysiology models. Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology, 107(1):11-20.
rows.model_type: cardiac cell electrophysiology ODE models (31 CellML models)
rows.controlled_mutations: no; compares existing published models, no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; model-independent protocol language applied S1-S2 restitution and L-type calcium current-voltage protocols across models.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; derived outputs such as restitution curves and I-V curves; cardiac quantities, not neuronal eFEL features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; protocols are standard and user-defined.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; models are characterised or compared, with no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted or automated model transformations are studied.
rows.software: Functional curation in Chaste (paper URL http://www.comlab.ox.ac.uk/chaste; current repo https://github.com/Chaste/Chaste)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Pioneers reusable protocols across models and suggests them for development regression. NeuroSem adds neuron-specific mutants, calibrated tolerances, compact battery selection, and held-out generalisation tests.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.pbiomolbio.2011.06.003; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 21704062); author preprint PDF at cs.ox.ac.uk (Unpaywall link from Europe PMC) read with pypdf; GitHub REST API for Chaste/Chaste.
rows.found_via: Google Scholar 'model testing against electrophysiological features'; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works

rows.citation: Daly AC, Clerx M, Beattie KA, et al. (2018). Reproducible model development in the cardiac electrophysiology Web Lab. Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology, 139:3-14.
rows.model_type: cardiac cell and ion-channel ODE models (CellML), including hERG model fitting
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no seeded faults; focus on fitting and comparison of competing models.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; Web Lab applies the same protocol collection to many models for side-by-side comparison.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; protocol post-processing outputs (e.g. APD, currents) and fitting to data; not neuronal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial; protocol design support is described as a planned WL2 capability, not a fault-detection battery optimiser.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; models are characterised or compared, with no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted or automated model transformations are studied.
rows.software: Cardiac Electrophysiology Web Lab https://github.com/ModellingWebLab (BSD 3-clause per paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Infrastructure for sharing protocols and comparing model versions. NeuroSem adds mutant-based measurement of what batteries detect, calibrated tolerances, greedy selection, and held-out evaluation for neurons.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.pbiomolbio.2018.05.011; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 29842853); PMC6288479 full-text XML via Europe PMC; GitHub REST API for ModellingWebLab/WebLab.

rows.citation: Mirams GR, Clerx M, Whittaker DG, et al. (2024). Optimal experimental designs for characterising ion channel gating by filling the phase-voltage space of model dynamics. Mathematics in Medical and Life Sciences, 1:2375494.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; optimises one short voltage-clamp waveform built from steps, not a battery of current-clamp protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; objective uses coverage of discretised phase-voltage space, not extracted electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes; CMA-ES optimises protocol parameters to maximise phase-voltage coverage while keeping protocols short.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; designed using one hERG model, identifiability then checked with synthetic data from a different Markov model.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted or automated model transformations are studied.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Optimises protocols for parameter information in ion-channel models. NeuroSem instead selects protocol subsets to maximise detection of seeded behavioural faults in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/29937574.2024.2375494; OpenAlex abstract and OA status; bioRxiv API and full text for 10.1101/2024.05.02.592179; Taylor & Francis page returned HTTP 403; GitHub REST API.
